configs.description: The TM-7124S as ordered: fan tray, one AC supply in PS1, a blank in PS2 and a blank in the expansion slot.
configs.name: base

configs.description: The base with a second AC supply (TM-7124S-ACPS) in PS2 for redundancy.
configs.name: dual-ac

configs.description: Two AC supplies and the LC-7124-2XFP-B in the expansion slot - how the 2025 render shows the TM-7124S.
configs.name: with-xfp-card

gaps.note: telco.com publishes data sheets only; hardware documentation is on a support portal behind a login, whose contact is on telco.com/support. Searched: the telco.com media library, every product and knowledge-centre page, and the Wayback index of telco.com PDFs.
gaps.wanted: the TM-7124S / T-Metro 7124S hardware installation guide, from the BATM support portal.

gaps.note: The 2022 NetZoom master puts the SFP blocks 6.8 mm, the CON/ETH stack 4 mm and the fan tray's left edge 2.8 mm to the right of where the 2025 render (rectified, about 1.6 px/mm) puts them, and the render's expansion card is 166 wide where the stencil's is 171.5. The supply bays, the DA-15 and the slot's left edge agree within 2.5 mm. The render is used for positions and is itself only good to about a millimetre.
gaps.wanted: a square-on photograph of the front at 4 px/mm or better.

gaps.note: The wide-range DC supply (TM-7124S-DCPS-W) is orderable but no image or stencil master draws its face, so it is not modelled and there is no DC configuration.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the DC supply's face.

gaps.note: The stencil master TM-7124S (R) draws the rear as a plain panel; no photograph confirms it.
No edition states the ETH port's rate; 1g is carried as a BORROWED value from the TM-8104 (see provenance.eth-speed), not as a finding.

The DC feed connector carries two feeds, A and B, but is one part and so exports one power port; a DCIM cannot cable the two feeds separately. Splitting it into two parts would draw one physical header as two.
gaps.wanted: an exporter convention for a multi-feed connector (two power rows from one part).

gaps.note: Two lamps per SFP port, and Sync, Fan, STS and EXT, are drawn where they are; no document says what any of their states mean.

gaps.wanted: a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

`attrs.platform.cpu`, `attrs.platform.memory`; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 4 bays (front 4); `physical-context` on port group sfp - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

alarm-port.note: "Alarm Input & Output" is a D-sub whose jackscrews stand 33.4 mm apart in the rectified render - the registry's DA-15 (33.32), not the HD-15 (25.0) - so it is std/da15@1. The stencil's shell is ambiguous between the two (24.1 wide, screws 28.4 apart).

chassis.note: 1.5RU, 440 x 66.3 x 253. Width and depth are the data sheets' ("440mm (19' racks) x 67mm (2.625') x 253mm (10')"); the height is not - see chassis-height.

chassis-height.note: 66.3, NOT the data sheet's 67. The height is 440 divided by the rendered face's MEASURED aspect, 6.64 - the render's four corners fix that ratio, and the stencil's body (441.4 x 66.2) agrees with it - against the data sheet's 67; the 0.7 mm between them is recorded rather than split.

controls.note: The Alarm Cut Off push button is drawn with common/reset-button@1, the nearest library part; the real button is a small square cap about 5 x 7 mm (render and stencil). Reset is a pinhole.

dc-feed.note: The four-pole green connector at the left end, legend -48VA RETA -48VB RETB, is on the chassis in both the AC and DC stencil masters and in the render (an AC build), so it is drawn on every configuration. The DC system is ordered "with DC feed connector".

eth-speed.note: BORROWED, NOT STATED. No edition gives the ETH management port's rate. 1g is taken from the TM-8104's OOB port - same vendor, same OS family and the same console-plus- Ethernet management stack - following the maintainer's ruling for unstated management rates; NetBox's community entry types the 8104's port 1000base-t, itself unsourced. The eth-speed gap stays open.

fan-tray.note: The data sheets ship a fan tray with every base system. The stencil draws it as a full-height module at the right end (40.85 x 64.66) with two corner thumbscrews and a pull window; the render shows the same. Its bay uses the stencil's position.

front-layout.note: TWO SOURCES THAT DISAGREE, EACH USED FOR WHAT IT DOES WELL. Positions are read off the 2025 render rectified by a four-corner homography onto the face (corners TL 83.5,155 TR 784.5,154.5 BR 784.5,260.5 BL 84.5,260.5; about 1.6 px/mm, so good to about a millimetre), then scaled 440/441.4 to the data sheet's body. Shapes, pitches and the legends come from the 2022 stencil master, which is AN OLDER BUILD: its supply bays, DA-15 and expansion-slot left edge agree with the render within 2.5 mm, but it draws the SFP blocks 6.8 mm further right, the CON/ETH stack 4 mm right and a different expansion card. Where they disagree on position the render - the current product - is used (see the stencil-vs-render gap).

jack-orientation.note: The ETH jack's lamp labels (LNK/ACT, MNG) are printed under it and its lamp windows sit on its lower corners in the render, so it is keyway-down (unrotated); CON above it is turned 180, belly to belly. CON carries no lamps, so the unlamped std/rj45-ganged@2 is used for it.

lamps.note: TWO ARROW LAMPS PER PORT. Each column carries two ▲▼ pairs in the strip between the rows - the stencil draws them at 1.55, 4.12, 7.88 and 10.46 mm from the column's left edge, and the render shows the same doubled pattern - so each port has two lamps (-a and -b), up-arrows for the upper port, down for the lower. What the two mean (likely link and activity) is not documented. Sync and Fan are round lamps and Reset a pinhole beside the DA-15; STS and EXT are small lamps over the CON/ETH stack.

model.note: TM-7124S data sheet (telco.com 2025/12, product page tm-7124); the 2016-08 and 2019-01 editions call it the T-Metro 7124S, which the face prints.

ports.note: 24 std/sfp@1 in three 2 x 4 blocks. The blocks start where the render puts them (x 190.0, 251.8, 313.5 before scaling); inside a block the columns are on the stencil's 14.72 pitch - individual cages with a 0.8 mm web, not a ganged block - which the render's block widths (57.6-58.9 for four columns) corroborate. Rows at y 10.85 and 26.35 (render centres); the lower row is turned 180. Numbered as printed, "△1 ▽2" over each column: the odd port above, the even below; "1/" before each block.

power.note: NOT STATED: no edition gives a consumption figure. Input: "100-240VAC, 50/60 Hz, -48VDC, -60VDC and +24VDC nominal"; the AC supply's face prints "100-240V~50-60Hz 2A".

sources.note: Three data-sheet editions (2016-08, 2019-01, 2025-12); three vendor renders, of which telco.com 2025/09/t-metro-7124s.png (858 px) is the only near-square one; and the legacy NetZoom stencil "Telco Systems" (2022), masters TM-7124S (F), (CF), (R), TM-7124S-DC (CF) and LC-7124-2XFB-B (MFS). No installation guide is public.

timing.note: "SyncE, IEEE 1588v2* PTP, BITS and phase clock" (2019 edition). The chassis face has no timing connector; the sync and phase clock jacks are on the LC-7124-2XFP-B card.
